source: White light is a mix of all the colors of the rainbow: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet. A prism or raindrops spread them out. A red apple looks red because it reflects red light.
Thinking a prism adds colors to light. The colors were already in the white light; the prism spreads them apart.
In 1666 young Isaac Newton made a hole in his window shutter and let a beam of sunlight through a glass prism. On the wall appeared a band of colors.

White light is a mix of all the colors: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet (the letters ROY G BIV help you remember). A prism, or raindrops, bend each color a different amount and spread them apart.
A prism spreads white light into a spectrum. Violet bends the most, red the least.
A rainbow appears when the Sun is behind you and rain is in front of you. Each raindrop acts like a tiny prism.

A red apple looks red because it reflects red light and soaks up the other colors. A white shirt reflects all colors; a black one soaks up nearly all of them, which is why black clothes get hot in the sun.
In a room lit only by red light, what color does a white sheet of paper look?
White paper reflects whatever light hits it.
Thinking the prism adds the colors. Newton showed the colors were in the sunlight already; a second prism can mix them back into white.
